newsitem.title: FINLAND: CULTOR SEES 96 EPS DOWN A QUARTER ON 95.
newsitem.headline: CULTOR SEES 96 EPS DOWN A QUARTER ON 95.

text.p: Finnish foodstuffs, animal feed and bakery group Cultor Oy said on Wednesday it expected its 1996 earnings per share to be about one quarter lower than the 1995 level, which was 14.91 markka.

"We now estimate the group's full-year result (earnings per share) in 1996 to be about one quarter lower than the corresponding figure of last year," Cultor said in a statement with its January-August results.
"The net sales of Cultor group are estimated to be approximately 8.5 billion in 1996," Cultor said. Its 1995 net sales were 6.20 billion markka.
Cultor, which on September 9 warned against "too high" result expectations, repeated on Wednesday that group profitability started to improve towards the end of the second tertial.
"July and August were substantially better than the previous months, and the trend is estimated to continue," Cultor said.
It said problems in raw material supply which had encumbered earnings in the first eight months were easing.
"The raw material supply situation has recovered towards the year-end and the business units have been able to improve their performance by adapting their activities," it said.
It said the integration of the Food Science Group, which Cultor bought from Pfizer at the start of the year, "presents a major challenge to the group in 1996".
But it said organisational restructuring and development had proceeded according to plan.
Cultor earlier said its January-August profit after financial items fell 42 percent to 196 million markka, with earnings per share almost halving to 5.55 markka from 10.24 markka.
